html:
The Trans-Gabon Railway runs about 650 kilometres from the port of Owendo near Libreville to Franceville in the southeast, and was built between 1974 and 1986.

It was the great project of Omar Bongo, paid for largely with oil money after the World Bank had doubted its value. It cut through rainforest to open the interior for timber and for the manganese of Moanda, which had until then gone out by cable car into Congo.

The line made Gabon one of the world's main manganese exporters and linked Franceville, Bongo's home region, to the capital. It is the only railway in the country, and its slow upkeep and accidents have been a long-running political issue in Gabon.
sum: The Trans-Gabon Railway runs about 650 kilometres from the port of Owendo near Libreville to Franceville in the southeast, and was built between 1974 and 1986.
